anchors.paper_title: MNE-BIDS: Organizing electrophysiological data into the BIDS format and facilitating their analysis
anchors.paper_venue: The Journal of Open Source Software
anchors.reason: MNE-BIDS is a software tool for organizing electrophysiology data into BIDS, used for formatting; it does not describe this paired-associates stimulation dataset.

anchors.paper_title: iEEG-BIDS, extending the Brain Imaging Data Structure specification to human intracranial electrophysiology
anchors.reason: iEEG-BIDS is a specification for organizing intracranial EEG data, which this BIDS dataset follows; it does not describe this paired-associates dataset.

metadata.methods_description: Each session comprised 25 lists of encoding (6 word pairs, 4000 ms each), arithmetic distractor, and cued recall (5000 ms per cue). Twenty lists per session were stimulation lists, 10 with stimulation at encoding and 10 at retrieval, on alternating pairs or cues, and 5 lists had no stimulation. Stimulation began 200 ms before stimulus onset and lasted 4.6 s. Stimulation parameters are recorded in the events files. Recordings were made with Blackrock or Medtronic systems, with monopolar and bipolar montages provided.
